stem: A hospitalized 78-year-old develops abrupt confusion, impaired attention, and disorganized thinking that fluctuate over the course of the day. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

options.A: This pattern is most consistent with uncomplicated dementia progression because dementia commonly changes markedly over hours within the same day.
options.B: This pattern is most consistent with normal cognitive aging because fluctuating attention and sudden confusion are expected during hospitalization.
options.C: This pattern is most consistent with delirium, an acute fluctuating disturbance that warrants prompt evaluation for an underlying medical, medication, substance, or other precipitating cause.
options.D: This pattern is most consistent with major depression alone because depression typically causes abrupt disorientation and fluctuating attention over hours.

rationale: Current StatPearls defines delirium as an acute disturbance of attention, awareness and cognition developing over a short period and fluctuating in severity. It also requires evidence of an underlying medical condition, substance exposure/withdrawal or other cause and emphasizes prompt identification and treatment of precipitating factors. C therefore fits the abrupt fluctuating inattention and confusion. Dementia is generally chronic/progressive, normal aging does not explain acute inattention, and depression alone does not best explain this fluctuating disorientation.
educational_objective: Recognize acute, fluctuating inattention and cognitive change in a hospitalized older adult as delirium and evaluate promptly for reversible precipitating causes.
source_locator: Continuing Education Activity; Introduction; DSM-5 criteria; Evaluation/management discussion emphasizing acute fluctuating attention/cognition and underlying causes.
source_claim_supported: Delirium is an acute, fluctuating disturbance of attention/awareness/cognition caused by an underlying condition, substance/toxin or related precipitant; early recognition and treatment of underlying causes are central.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation — acute/complex alterations and medical emergencies, detailed content pp. 42-44.

source_original.stem: A hospitalized 78-year-old develops abrupt confusion, impaired attention, and disorganized thinking that fluctuate over the course of the day. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

options.A: This pattern is most consistent with uncomplicated dementia progression, because dementia commonly changes markedly over hours within the same day.
options.B: This pattern is most consistent with normal cognitive aging, because fluctuating attention and sudden confusion are expected during hospitalization.
options.C: This pattern is most consistent with delirium, an acute disturbance that warrants prompt evaluation for an underlying medical or medication-related cause.
options.D: This pattern is most consistent with major depression alone, because depression typically causes abrupt disorientation and fluctuating attention over hours.

source_original.rationale: Delirium is characterized by an acute change in attention and cognition with a fluctuating course. Option C is correct because the sudden, variable confusion warrants evaluation for an underlying medical or medication-related cause. Option A incorrectly describes the abrupt hourly fluctuation as uncomplicated dementia progression. Option B incorrectly normalizes sudden confusion as expected aging or hospitalization. Option D attributes the pattern to depression alone even though abrupt disorientation and fluctuating attention point to delirium.
source_original.source_detail: Continuing Education/Introduction and Evaluation/DSM criteria: delirium is an acute disturbance of attention/awareness and cognition developing over a short period with a fluctuating course; evaluate for underlying medical, medication, substance, or environmental causes. StatPearls Delirium updated 2026-01-10; current NCBI Bookshelf version rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Physiological Adaptation: acute/complex alterations, medical emergencies and pathophysiologic adaptation. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained key and construct. Expanded the cause wording beyond medical/medication to match the current DSM-based StatPearls description of medical conditions, substances/withdrawal or toxins without adding a specific unprovided cause.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Acute onset, fluctuating course, inattention/cognition and underlying cause requirement are directly supported.

distractor_audit.A: Dementia is generally chronic/progressive, not abrupt fluctuating hourly change.
distractor_audit.B: Acute inattention/confusion is not normal aging.
distractor_audit.D: Depression alone does not best fit fluctuating attention/disorientation.

audit_findings.cueing: All options are cognitive/psychiatric interpretations; no second answer.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Cross-checked with June 2026 StatPearls delirium-vs-dementia update; no conflict remains.
